newsitem.title: USA: Farrakhan blames Catholics Church for hate crimes. [CORRECTED 21:48 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Farrakhan blames Catholics Church for hate crimes. [CORRECTED 21:48 GMT]

text.p: Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan on Sunday blamed Catholics for a series of racial attacks and defended himself against charges of being an anti-Semite.
Farrakhan said on NBC's "Meet the Press" (Corrects show)
that he planned to address an ecumenical meeting in Philadelphia planned for this week despite the withdrawal in protest against him by Jewish and Catholic representatives.

"If I might respectfully say, Mayor (Ed) Rendell is Jewish," Farrakhan said. "He invited me to the city. I hope to speak to that condition, and I would hope that the Catholic Church would not fasten on words while we could fasten on deeds."

"Do you know that the young men (who) ran out and beat up that young lady in Philadelphia came out of a Catholic Church?" Farrakhan said of a beating incident involving a black woman, her son and nephew.
He also accused Catholics of similar attacks in Bridgeport, Connecticut, and in Chicago.
"I am called a hate teacher, a hate preacher, an anti- Semite, a bigot and nobody wants to talk with me because it doesn't appear that I have love in my heart," he said.

"But look, in the 20 years that I have been the leader of the Nation of Islam, there is not one single incident of any Moslem being arrested for a hate crime," Farrakhan said. "Yet the (Catholic) church is the bastion of love, but all of this hate is coming toward us out of the church."
He stood by comments that he made criticising "big Jews" for allegedly financing Adolph Hitler who ordered the deaths of "little Jews."
"My problem with the Jewish community is, is that most of the people feel -- or the Jewish people feel -- that if you criticise any act of Jews, that is anti-Semitic," Farrakhan said.
"If I criticise Arabs, if I criticise the government of the United States, if I criticise white people or my own black people, I'm not considered anti-black, anti-Arab," he said.
